title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
slides: Why is your AI assistant pointing you to fake stores?
A new study tested five major chatbots for retail recommendations.
Up to 30% of links led to nonexistent or fraudulent sites.
Always verify the URL before clicking a chatbot's suggestion.
Next time, cross-check with a direct search.
thread_text:
1. Fake stores in results

A new study tested five major chatbots for retail recommendations and found up to 30% of links led to nonexistent or fraudulent sites.

2. The test setup

Researchers prompted each chatbot with common shopping queries and then checked every URL they returned against live, verified retailers.

3. Why this happens

Chatbots generate plausible-sounding links from patterns, not live web checks, so a fake store can slip through with a believable name.

4. The real risk

Clicking one of these links can expose your payment details or install malware before you notice anything wrong with the storefront.

5. Verify before you click

Next time a chatbot suggests a store, copy the URL and search it directly. Does the domain match the brand you actually trust?

instagram.caption:
Up to 30% of the retail links five major chatbots gave researchers pointed to stores that don't exist or are outright fraudulent.

Researchers asked the bots common shopping questions, then checked every URL against verified live retailers. A third of them failed the test.

The bots build links from patterns, not live web checks — so a fake store with a believable name slips through. One click can expose your payment details or install malware.

If you publish or shop online, treat every chatbot link as unverified until you've checked it yourself.

Next time a bot names a store, copy the URL and search it directly. Does the domain match the brand? 🔍
